verdict.rationale: FireHydrant publishes an API reference (docs.firehydrant.com/reference, with per-endpoint pages and a developers portal) covering the full UI surface, and an OpenAPI 3.0.1 document exists in the official MCP repo. Nothing in the evidence shows the reference is interactive or has runnable 'try it' examples, and probes for an OpenAPI spec on the docs site returned 404. missing for 10: evidence of interactive in-browser request execution, runnable code examples per endpoint, a publicly discoverable OpenAPI spec on the docs site, hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: You can use the FireHydrant API to configure integrations, define incidents, and set up webhooks--anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI.
Note that the read-only endpoint has a much longer timeout for retrieving more complex data, but may lag behind the primary endpoint by as much as 30s.
publishes a FireHydrant OpenAPI document (.speakeasy/openapi.output.yaml): openapi "3.0.1"
